decisions.issues: Acceptable. The beat works: joined hands in the foreground, Revathi's face lifting toward Nagoji, same night room with the barred window and plank door. Nagoji has the curled moustache, a clean chin (faint shading only) and the gold stud. The brand and scar are on his near LEFT forearm, which is the correct arm. The script's night look is cream dhoti, ribs bound and a cream shoulder cloth, which panel 7.3 needs. This matches 6.5 but not 7.3. Clean. Revathi is close, in the same room with the barred window, palms and plank door. decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition and setting. Revathi kneels at left in the indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, coin necklace and gold armlets. Second, the action: Revathi's LEFT hand, with its gold bangles, has traced up his bare right arm and her fingertips rest on his bare right shoulder. Nagoji's own LEFT hand reaches across his chest and closes firmly around her wrist just below the bangles. decisions.issues: v01 is rejected. (1) The brand, drawn as a rosette patch, and the long white scar are on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the near arm of a figure facing right, on its outer top surface. decisions.correction: Keep this composition. decisions.issues: v01 is rejected. Nagoji, seen from behind in the foreground, wears a frayed, torn sleeveless tunic that reads as his captivity rags. decisions.correction: Keep this over-the-shoulder composition and Revathi exactly as drawn: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, chin lifted, defiant with a question under it. decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): Nagoji has a clear grey streak at the temple. The script calls for no grey anywhere on pages 3 to 9. Her necklace is a string of flat gold coins, not round beads. decisions.correction: Nagoji is in his convalescent night look, not the commander sheet. decisions.issues: Minor: the foreground lamp is a taller brass stand lamp than the small lamp in 8.3. Both are brass oil lamps with open wicks, so it is acceptable. The two clothed silhouettes merging on the wall are the intended implied beat. There is no text or nudity. Minor only. They are propped against the wall rather than lying flat on the mat, but the embrace reads clearly: her head is on his shoulder, he holds his ribs, and she can sit up from this in 9.3. Nagoji matches the script costume: bare chest, white rib binding, plain cream shoulder cloth, dhoti, loose hair, no grey, flush ear stud and thick moustache. That is technically the outer side, but it is small and incidental. Revathi matches her sheet with the pallu over her shoulder and no tali. The upper right wall is clear for both balloons.

Wrong costume: the main figure wears a cream long-sleeved tunic with rolled sleeves and a red sash or shoulder cloth, which is the commander look. It should show bare chest, rib binding and a plain shoulder cloth as in 9.1. The frame paints its own bordered picture-in-picture inset instead of being a single inset shot. Grey shows in his hair, which breaks 9.1 and the art direction of no grey on page 9. The brand and scar sit on the forearm planted on the mat, which reads as his RIGHT arm, and the brand is drawn as a flower or cross-like patch.
decisions.correction: This panel is itself the small inset, so draw ONE close shot only: no painted sub-panel, frame, border or picture-in-picture anywhere. Show Nagoji close, head and shoulders, half-reclined on the woven mat in the same earth cellar and warm single-lamp light as 9.1. He is caught mid-laugh as the pain hits: mouth still open from the laugh, eyes squeezed and brow knotting into a wince, his RIGHT hand pressed flat against his side. Costume exactly as 9.1: bare chest and arms, a band of white linen rib binding wound around his ribs, a plain undecorated cream shoulder cloth over his left shoulder and a cream dhoti. No tunic, no sleeves, no red sash or red cloth of any kind. Hair loose, long, curly and fully black with no grey. Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud. Keep his left forearm out of frame so no brand or scar shows. Keep the upper third of the frame plain dark earth wall and timber for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Nagoji wears the torn ochre sleeveless captivity tunic. That costume belongs to chapters 1 to 4 and breaks 9.1, where he has a bare chest, white rib binding, plain shoulder cloth and dhoti. Revathi herself is good: sitting up on the mat in the indigo sari, serious, looking down at him.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is NOT in captivity rags: no ochre tunic, no torn shirt and no shirt of any kind. Draw him exactly as in 9.1: bare chest and arms, a band of white linen rib binding wound around his ribs, a plain undecorated cream shoulder cloth over his left shoulder and a cream dhoti. Hair loose, long, curly and fully black with no grey. Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud. He lies back on the mat propped on his right elbow, looking up at her, with his left forearm tucked under him or turned away so no brand or scar shows. Keep Revathi as drawn in this version: sitting up on the woven mat in the indigo sari with gold borders, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and sandalwood line, one hand drawing the pallu back over her shoulder, looking down at him with a serious face. Keep the same cellar, door, timber ceiling and small brass lamp, and keep the band of plain earth wall above their heads clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with the pallu over her shoulder, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, and no tali or red dot. She wears a small private smile and glances to the right, toward where Nagoji lay in 9.3. The same cellar door and timber ceiling show. The lamp is a tall standing brass lamp rather than the small one in 9.1. That is a minor difference and is acceptable in a close-up background. The upper right wall between her head and the door is clear for both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel to the right.

Shows the beat: Nagoji alone, sitting up on the mat and looking at the low door, with dawn in thin blades through its cracks. The brass lamp is out with one thread of smoke rising, and the other half of the mat is empty. Minor drift: a few faint grey strands at the temple (no grey is wanted on page 9). His shoulder cloth has a gold border, where 9.1 has a plain one. The rib binding is hidden under the draped cloth. The brand sits high near the elbow on the visible face of the forearm, small at panel scale. The large plain wall in the upper middle holds both captions.

The lamp has a live flame, but the script and 9.5 call for a cold, burned-out lamp. Nagoji's arm comes out of a rolled cream tunic sleeve with a red sash, the commander look, where 9.1 and 9.5 show a bare arm with dhoti and shoulder cloth. The cellar door stands open on outdoor daylight, against 9.5's closed door with light through the cracks. The brand is drawn large on the outer forearm, and its ridges form letter-like shapes that verge on pseudo-writing.
decisions.correction: The lamp is cold: a small brass dish lamp with a dead, blackened wick, no flame and no glow, matching the burned-out lamp of 9.5. Nagoji's arm is bare from the shoulder: no tunic, no sleeve, no rolled cloth, no red sash or red cloth anywhere. Only the edge of his cream dhoti and a plain cream shoulder cloth may show at the frame edge. Draw his LEFT hand resting palm down on the empty half of the woven mat, close beside the cold lamp. Frame tight on the hand, wrist and lower forearm, with the forearm turned so no brand, scar, ridges or marks of any kind show. The low wooden door in the corner stays SHUT, with only thin blades of grey-gold dawn light through its cracks, as in 9.5: no open doorway, no outdoors, no sky. Keep the wide empty mat, the cool dawn light, the earth wall and timber ceiling, and keep the plain upper wall band clear for one caption.

decisions.issues: v01 sets the scene well: wet mossy river steps, clear river, rows of brass ghee lamps, a Kerala temple wall, and Nagoji barefoot in rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash with a clean chin, gold stud and no grey. The problem is Varma, the bare-chested man in white at the head of the party. He has a prominent grey streak at the temple, loose shoulder-length curls and a gold ear stud, so he reads as Nagoji's later-life sheet rather than the V13 Varma face. That breaks the grey-as-clock rule the page header sets up, because readers will take the grey as Nagoji's. It also clashes with the black-haired Varma in 10.2 to 10.5.
decisions.correction: Draw Marthanda Varma, the bare-chested man in the plain white cloth at the head of the party, from the V13 varma-v1 sheet, and make sure he does not resemble Nagoji. Give him jet-black hair with NO grey or silver streak anywhere, gathered in a knot above his LEFT ear, not loose shoulder-length curls. Use the V13 Varma face (a longer, narrower jaw, curled moustache, red-and-white Vaishnavite forehead mark). He wears no earrings, no gold ear stud and no jewellery, and a narrow linen dressing on his left shoulder sits half hidden under the white cloth. Keep everything else as it is: the wet, mossy black stone steps running into the clear river, the rows of brass ghee lamps along the temple wall, the white royal parasol and the barefoot attendants behind, and Nagoji walking barefoot at Varma's side in rust-red turban, cream tunic with pushed-up sleeves and broad red sash, with a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud and no grey at the temples. Leave the open sky at upper right clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The left-shoulder dressing is not visible because it is the far shoulder under the cloth, which reads as 'half hidden'. There is a faint touch of grey at Varma's sideburn. The tall brass lamp stands read slightly like candles. The beat is clear: barefoot, no crown or jewels, plain white cloth, gold and pepper sacks laid before the dark inner shrine. The dark upper-left hall gives clean caption space.

v01 has the right beat and a good priest: the V13 temple priest carries the sword across both palms toward Varma's open hands, in a dark granite corridor with a lit sanctum. But Varma wears two long strands of gold bead necklaces. The sword has a diamond-wrapped black grip and a ring/disc guard that reads as a Japanese or European hybrid, not a Kerala royal blade, and it does not match the plain gilt hilt in 10.4.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma wears NO jewellery in this panel: no gold bead necklaces, no chains, no earrings. He wears only the plain white cloth over his left shoulder, with a narrow linen dressing half hidden beneath it, exactly as in the neighbouring panels where he kneels at the shrine and rides home. Draw his face from the V13 varma-v1 sheet as a mature man in his thirties, not a youth, with black hair in a knot and the Vaishnavite forehead mark. The sword is a long, straight Kerala royal blade with a plain gilt brass hilt: round pommel, short straight crossguard and a plain dark grip, with no braided or diamond-wrapped grip and no ring or disc guard. Keep everything else: the priest from the V13 temple-priest sheet carrying the sword flat across both open palms and laying it into Varma's cupped hands, the dark granite corridor with the lamp-lit inner sanctum behind, the brass oil lamps with open wicks, and a dark, low-detail band at the top of the frame for the caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's hair is loose curls with a small topknot rather than the knot of 10.2, and he has a leather riding shoe in the stirrup. Kayal's black lower legs are out of frame, but her bay coat and black mane match. Nagoji is on the sheet (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, no grey) and is watching Varma. Varma has no crest and no jewels and holds the sheathed straight sword across his lap with both hands. The green paddy country is right, and the upper-centre and upper-right sky hold both captions clear of faces.

v01 is framed as a medium-wide of Varma riding toward camera, not the scripted narrow strip where the sword's edge is the subject and the riders are small. It brings in continuity breaks. The blade is a curved drawn sabre, where 10.3 and 10.4 establish a long straight sword. Varma's horse is a bay with a white blaze, where 10.4 has a dark horse. Nagoji and Kayal, who ride at his side in 10.4, are missing. Varma's face is drawn without his sheet (cast was empty) and lacks the Vaishnavite mark of 10.2.
decisions.correction: Make the blade the subject, not the rider. Show a tight close-up of the same long, straight royal sword (plain gilt brass hilt with round pommel and short straight crossguard, dark grip, straight blade with a tapered point) lying bare across Varma's knees on his plain white cloth, his hands resting lightly on it and no face in frame. The sun flares in one bright point along its edge, and the black mane of his dark horse shows at the lower edge. Behind it, far away and small on the red laterite road through the green paddy fields and palms, comes the column of riders: Nagoji's rust-red turban on his bay mare Kayal near the front, white-turbaned riders with spears behind. Keep the sunlit paddy, the hills and the wide clear sky on the right for the caption. No curved sabre, no drawn-and-raised blade, no bay horse with a white blaze under Varma.

decisions.issues: Minor: Lannoy stands just behind Ramayyan at the table rather than clearly apart beside it, and has a faint white rim outline. Both principals match their sheets (Lannoy in white tunic-coat over white mundu, not blue). Caption space: open sky top centre-right (x 0.62-0.88, y 0-0.15) and wall above the awning top-left.

Framing departs from the script: Nagoji is a large over-the-shoulder foreground figure on the left rather than a small figure on a bastion lip, and he looks across more than down. The high angle over angled, sloped star-trace bastions (under construction, matching the half-built parapet in 11.4) still carries the beat. Clean. Tall square-cornered Deccan fort on a crag in dry ochre colours. The unlettered saffron swallow-tailed pennant suits a memory panel. Wide open sky top-left for the caption.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (white tunic-coat, white mundu, sandals, pale hair with a black ribbon) and is kneeling, tracing angled lines in wet clay with a stick. The squat, heavy mason ponders the sketch. The clay drawing has no letters. Open sky top centre-right (x 0.42-0.98, y 0-0.13) holds both Lannoy balloons.

The mason is a different man from the one in 11.4, and the setting does not carry over. decisions.correction: The mason MUST be the same man as in panel 11.4: a squat, very heavy-set, broad-bellied Kerala mason with massive arms like tree trunks, a thick full black beard, black curly hair bound by a plain cream cloth headband (not a wrapped turban, no hanging tail), bare-chested, a cream towel with thin red stripes over his left shoulder and a plain off-white mundu. No necklace, no red waistband, no hammer in hand. Set it in the same place and light as 11.4: on top of the half-built granite parapet, with the patch of smoothed wet clay and its angled sketch lines at their feet, bamboo scaffolding and coconut palms beyond, under the same bright midday sky. Keep the composition that worked: the mason on the LEFT, frowning and unconvinced, one broad palm flat on an old square-cornered section of wall beside the parapet; Lannoy on the RIGHT (same white tunic-coat, white ankle-length mundu, sandals, pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon) now fully upright, bending slightly to brush clay dust off the knees of his mundu with one hand. Leave clear open sky above each man's head for the two balloons (mason first, then Lannoy).

decisions.issues: Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale wavy hair with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat over a white mundu, sandals. He stands before a line of bare-chested Nair musketeers in dhotis drilling with upright muskets, with a cannon crew beyond. Hands are sound and there is no text. Nagoji wears a buttoned blue Travancore drill coat over his tunic. The script and bible allow the blue coat only on parade day (14.2), and 12.2 is an ordinary afternoon drill. A grey streak shows at his temple, but the script's grey schedule has none from 10.1 to 14.3 and 12.2 says 'no grey yet'. With both sleeves rolled, a long white scar shows on the RIGHT (sword-arm) forearm as well as the left, but brand and scar belong only on the inner LEFT forearm. Megha (dappled grey, black mane and tail), the riders wheeling on sand, and the sky are good.
decisions.correction: Nagoji wears NO blue coat in this panel. The blue Travancore drill coat is for parade day only (14.2), and this is an ordinary afternoon drill. Dress him exactly on the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic with both sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash over the shoulder and round the waist, cream trousers, boots, talwar in his right hand. His long curly hair is entirely black with NO grey or silver at the temples. Give him a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. Neither forearm shows any scar, brand or mark. Keep Megha exactly as drawn: a dappled grey with a black mane and tail, in full stride on the sand. Keep the afternoon drill ground with the fort wall, palms, open sky and the troop of Travancore horse wheeling in a loose circle around him with raised talwars. decisions.correction: Nagoji must wear his wrapped rust-red turban exactly as in the neighbouring parapet panels of pages 16 and 17, with long curly black hair and faint grey at the temples showing below it and a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe. Never draw him bare-headed in this scene. Keep his cream tunic sleeves rolled to mid-forearm as on pages 16 and 17, but fold his arms so only the outer backs of both forearms face the camera, clean and unmarked: no brand, scar, tattoo, pattern or discoloured patch on either forearm or near either elbow. Keep everything else that worked: the same sunset laterite bastion with the cannon embrasure, the small sailing boats on the inlet and palms beyond; Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals with his hand on the parapet, turning back from the water to speak; Nagoji facing him squarely with arms folded; and open sky above both men for the lettering. Keep both lower corners as plain, low-detail stone floor and parapet shadow with no crates, barrels or coiled rope, so the storm inset can sit there.

decisions.issues: Minor: where the rope fails, near the hull, the frayed strands bunch into a lump that could, looked at closely, be read as a small knot. At inset size it reads as the wet, fraying break the script asks for. The line is otherwise straight and taut and runs out of frame at top right, with no loop or noose. The hand is anatomically sound and slips from the line in a torn grey-brown sleeve (Keshavrao's colour). There is no face, no figure, no blood and no text, and the cold storm palette is right.

Minor only. The background Nair guards carry spears and wear their topknots on the crown rather than tied forward. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead rather than a perfectly flush stud, the same as in the accepted page 16 and 17 frames. Everything the beat needs is present: Udayagiri's granite hill, the new angled bastions, the wall walk, the ditch, and scrub with one small muzzle flash and puff of smoke at right. Lannoy (white coat and mundu, sandals) points along the wall and Nagoji (rust-red turban, commander dress, clean chin, faint grey) walks beside him. The large dusk sky at upper right leaves clear room for both captions. No text, and the hands are sound. The frame is 1536 px wide; as the script notes, it needs a 2x upscale to reach 300 PPI at full width.

Framing is a chest-up close shot rather than truly tight on the ear. The lifting strand is a few loose locks trailing off the far side of his head, where his hidden right ear is, which is subtle but readable with 18.3 and 18.5 on either side. His sidelong, half-startled look fits 'not yet understood'. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale wavy hair with black ribbon, long nose, white stand-collar tunic-coat). The background guards are bare-chested here but wear sleeveless white tunics in 18.3, a small inconsistency in incidental figures. No text, no gore.

Minor. The spray of stone chips bursts from the parapet top level with Nagoji's shoulder, not near his knee as scripted; it still clearly shows a shot striking the parapet beside him. A plain white pennant flies on the wall at upper left. It has no text but could faintly suggest a flag of truce, and it does not appear in 18.3. Otherwise sound. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, faint grey) drags Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) down behind the parapet. The hands are anatomically correct, and the outer left forearm correctly shows no brand. The sky above and right of the turban gives room for the short 'Down!' balloon without covering a face.

The beat is there (sentries scattering below the wall, muskets, two barking dogs, a man blowing a whistle, torches running for the ditch, empty scrub, clear sky for the caption). The problem is the biggest figure in the frame, the foreground sentry. He wears a dark rust-red/maroon turban, a cream tunic and a red sash, which are Nagoji's signature colours, and the whistle-blower is dressed the same way. Both are bearded. Coming straight after 18.5, the foreground man reads as a bearded Nagoji, who should not be in this panel and must be clean-chinned. The sentries also don't match 19.2, where the same sentries wear white turbans with a red band. The foreground musket's lock is unclear: there is no clear flint cock or frizzen, and a side bar looks like a later breech-loader's lever.
decisions.correction: Keep the dusk scene below the fort wall exactly as composed: torches running for the ditch, the two barking dogs, a man blowing a whistle, muskets being snatched up, the empty scrub and rocks beyond, and the open upper sky left clear for the caption. Dress every sentry as in the next panel (19.2): white or off-white turbans with at most a thin red band, a white tunic and a red waist sash. No rust-red, maroon or dark-red turban appears on anyone, so no sentry can be mistaken for Nagoji, who is NOT in this panel. Make the nearest foreground sentry clearly a different man from Nagoji: white turban, no talwar, musket in hand. All muskets are 1740s flintlocks with a visible flint cock and frizzen on the lock plate and a wooden ramrod under the barrel. No levers, hinged breech blocks, percussion caps or modern sights.

decisions.issues: Clean. An open palm (anatomy sound, thumb plus four fingers) holds three torn paper cartridge twists with black powder grains, with no casings or brass. It is torchlit by the bank below the wall, and the open dark sky at top left takes the caption. Minor: the grass is not obviously trampled, and the sentries wear white turbans with red bands rather than a distinctly Nair look; the current 19.1 does not match this, and the 19.1 correction asks it to.

Otherwise strong. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm leaves and stylus, seated by the lamp). Lannoy is in the white coat, mundu and sandals with his pale hair ribboned, apart, turning the chipped stone. Nagoji stands by the door with the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey at the temples, red sash and talwar. There is good dark wall space for three balloons. The failure is Nagoji's bare, crossed forearms: on the LEFT forearm's visible outer face, a white scar runs ACROSS the arm through a horizontal mottled patch. Together they read as a cross-shaped mark. The bible says the scar runs along the forearm from wrist toward elbow, beside a brand on the INNER forearm that is 'not a cross'.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, guardroom, lamplight and all three figures unchanged: Ramayyan seated with his palm-leaf bundles and stylus, Lannoy apart in his white coat and mundu turning the chipped parapet stone, Nagoji standing by the door with arms folded. Change only Nagoji's sleeves. His cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists and stay down, so no forearm skin shows and NO scar, brand, slash, cross or mark of any kind is visible on either arm. Keep his rust-red turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, broad red sash and talwar exactly as they are.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The setting is a morning audience in an open pillared hall. Varma is bare-headed with a knot above and behind his left ear, no turban or crest, bare-chested, with gold necklaces and a cream-and-gold cloth, stern and gesturing as he speaks. Nagoji matches his sheet (rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples). His visible forearm is unmarked and his left arm is out of view. Lannoy is in the white coat, mundu and sandals. Two bare-chested guards in white mundus flank the frame with curved swords; the right one also has a round shield. Hands are sound. Minor: the guards' topknots are tied high on the crown rather than forward-tied. The left guard's shield is out of view. Varma's hair is curlier than on the V13 sheet, and he wears a gold stud rather than pearl drops. Varma's two balloons fit over the ceiling beams at top centre and right.

Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples, unmarked forearms) and Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) are good, leaving the same hall as in 19.4, and the upper hall and courtyard have caption space. The two Nair guards are wrong. They carry SPEARS instead of the swords the script calls for. They also wear a white upper cloth over one shoulder, red waist sashes and sandals. In 19.4, where the script fixes their look for pages 19 to 21, they are bare-chested in plain white mundus with no sash and carry long curved swords, one with a round shield. Nagoji's talwar hilt also has a disc guard like a Japanese tsuba.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji, Lannoy, the pillared hall, the brass lamps, the morning courtyard light and the walking composition exactly as they are. Change only the two Nair guards walking a few paces behind, to match the guards established in panel 19.4. Each carries a long curved Nair sword held point-down in the right hand and a small round black shield with brass bosses on the left arm. There are NO spears, lances or poles anywhere in the panel. Both are bare-chested with NO upper or shoulder cloth, wear only a plain white mundu with no red sash or coloured border, and go barefoot with no sandals. Their hair is in a high Kerala topknot, they have moustaches and scarred forearms, and they wear no sacred thread or forehead marks. Nagoji's talwar keeps the Indian disc-pommel hilt from his sheet, with no tsuba-like guard.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch16 row: rust-red turban, red sash, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, first grey at the temples. The Nair shadow stands a few paces off with topknot, white cloth, sword and round shield, but wears a toga-like shoulder drape where 20.4 shows him bare-chested with a narrow shoulder cloth. The left-forearm brand is drawn as a small fern-like branching mark near the elbow, with no long white scar beside it. Panels 20.2 and 20.4 show a round puckered patch plus the scar. It is not letters or a cross and is tiny at print size; retouch it if convenient. There is a large clear dusk sky at upper right for both captions.

Minor only. Closer shot of Nagoji at the parapet, gazing right toward the dark hills, left hand resting on the stone. Face is on model with clean chin, curled moustache, stud and grey temples. The forearm shows the puckered patch and long white scar, matching 20.4. The tiny background Nair carries a spear and a cross-strap instead of the sword seen in 20.1 and 20.4; he is barely visible. Same dusk wall and lighting as 20.1 and 20.4. There is a large clear sky at upper right for the caption.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, gold armlets, the sheet's gold necklace, sandalwood line, and no tali, which is correct before ch20. She stands speaking openly in a pillared Kerala hall before seated listeners. The lamps are brass with open wicks, and there is no text. Plain plastered wall above and to the right of her head (about x 0.40 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.35) and at upper left holds the caption.

Minor only. Nagoji steps away from the parapet, his left hand just off the stone. His body turns from the hills while his head still glances back toward them, which reads as the turning moment. His face is on model. The left forearm shows the pale puckered brand and long white scar with no letters and no gore. Behind him the Nair shadow stands with weight shifted: topknot, bare chest, white mundu, sword in hand, round shield. Same dusk wall as 20.1 and 20.2. There is clear sky at upper right and above the walls at upper left for the two captions.

Minor: the two Nair shadows at far left carry spears with their round shields instead of the long Nair sword fixed at 19.4 and shown in 20.1 and 21.2. They are small and half cropped, so this is a small prop mismatch, not a reason to reject. Everything else matches: Lannoy fits his sheet (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat over a white mundu, sandals). Nagoji has the rust-red turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a gold ear stud, first grey at the temples, sash, talwar and boots. The test cannon fires from the lower battery, with smoke over the water and birds bursting from the trees. Hands are sound and there is no text. The upper-right dusk sky (about x 0.45 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.27) is open space for all three balloons.

Framing does not match the script. 21.2 calls for a wide shot with the men small against the sky. Here Nagoji and Lannoy are a medium walking two-shot filling about two-thirds of the frame height. That nearly repeats 21.1 (same pair, same wall, same dusk, Nairs at left) and loses the page's pull-back before the close. Likenesses, costumes and the Nair shadows (topknots, white mundus, sword and round shield) are otherwise correct. Also: a plain blank white flag on the tower could read as a surrender flag.
decisions.correction: Pull the camera far back into a true wide shot. The four figures stand small on the southern wall walk in the lower third of the frame, each no taller than about one fifth of the frame height, seen from a distance in profile or three-quarter back view as they look out toward the setting sun. Nagoji reads by his rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash and boots. Lannoy reads by his pale hair and white tunic-coat over a white mundu. The two Nair shadows (bare-chested, topknots, white mundus, a long sword and a round shield each) stand a few paces behind them. Keep the warm last-light palette, the stone bastions, palms, river and hills of 21.1 and this version. Give the whole upper half of the frame to open, softly graded sunset sky with only thin cloud, so three captions can sit there. Show no flag, or only Travancore's silver conch on red, and never a plain white flag.

decisions.issues: The marching soldiers are sliced off at the waist by the parapet coping. Their legs are in front of the wall, yet the wall top passes in front of their upper bodies, which is spatially impossible. The muskets are carried low across the body in the hand, not shouldered as the script asks. The bare feet, dhotis, dusk light and fort setting are right.
decisions.correction: Make the crop with the frame edge, not with the wall. Camera low and close at knee height, with the strip's top edge cutting the soldiers at the waist so no heads or upper bodies appear. Five or six barefoot soldiers in white dhotis march past left to right in step and in neat order. Each figure is whole and continuous and stands entirely in front of the parapet; no wall, coping, lamp or object passes in front of any body. Each carries a flintlock musket at the shoulder in the eighteenth-century manner: the left hand cups the butt at hip height and the stock and barrel rise steeply upward out of the top edge of the frame. The musket is never held low or horizontal across the body. Keep the dusk light, the stone flagstones and the fort wall behind them. Leave the left quarter of the strip as plain, shadowed parapet wall and flagstone with no figure in it, for the two captions.
